utterances.text: One second, Mr. Tieger. Witness, there's no need to seek eye contact either with the Defence or the accused. I noticed that when entering the courtroom your first concern was to greet Defence and accused before you -- with your eyes, with your gestures. I invite you to refrain from doing that and rather focus on questions, answers, and the Court. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As I was about --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Don't I have the right to address the Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are instructed to refrain from seeking eye contact even during examination by the Prosecution. Rather, focus on what Mr. Tieger asks you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As I advised my friends during the break, I would be --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- summarising the testimony given, giving them an opportunity to follow it. But because it's in English, I didn't consider it necessary to -- for the witness to have to track it word by word. Witness -- General, this witness provided the following information about what happened between the 28th of May and the 2nd of June. Testifying that on the 30th of May, 1992, Serbian Radio Zvornik broadcast that all citizens from the Drinjaca-Kostijerovo area requested to stay at home and not panic because the army will arrive. About an hour later, soldiers arrived. About 150 men, women, and children -- and that's found at e-court pages 10 and 11. About 150 men, women, and children rounded up, told to form a column, and taken to the Dom Kulture in Drinjaca, e-court pages 12 through 13. It was jam packed with hundreds of Muslims, that's at 14. And they were told by an officer, a uniformed officer that they were going to be transferred to some villages near Zenica and that Serbs would take their former homes. Only women and children would leave, while men would remain to be interviewed, e-court page 15. Approximately 90 men were murdered at the Dom Kulture, e-court pages 28 and 31. And similarly another statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But for this one I think out of an abundance of caution we should perhaps move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, General, to recap, I just provided you with the information that on June 1 another example of a village being surrounded, its population rounded up, the men separated from the women and children, taken to a facility wherein in that case many were murdered. Now, as I indicated, these events occurred in Zvornik in late May or the beginning of June 1992. Do you confirm these events, dispute these events, or say you simply don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer. The interpreters could not catch it. Perhaps you come a little bit closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As a general matter, however, General, you would acknowledge that forced displacement and killings took place in Zvornik subsequent to the orders to move out the Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about the forced departure of the Muslim population from Kozluk. You're aware of that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I am aware of it by reading about it in the papers, and I keep saying that but it seems that it's not doing any good. The brigade general didn't -- commander didn't have any responsibilities regarding the Birac Brigade, so I don't know why you are putting things to me that have nothing do with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You're the brigade commander of an important unit of the East Bosnia Corps, and in the adjacent municipality where a sister brigade is operating the Muslim population is being forcibly displaced consistent with an order that you gave and an order given by the Birac government, and you don't consider that in any way, shape, or form any part of your responsibility or interest, General?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. I don't have any responsibility in that regard, not even a minimal degree of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You have already indicated to this Court you were aware of liquidations of the Muslims in Zvornik; correct? Because you claim that was, in part, what prompted your order of the 31st of May.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Evidently we're going back to the same thing, and I have to repeat, Your Honours, other than what we stated before, a large number of Serbs from Tuzla, Zvornik, and Zivinice came. They were desperate. They were angry, and it was our problem how to protect those Muslims from being exposed to revenge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, General. You are off --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you were asking of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You were aware in May and June of 1992 that Muslims who were rounded up, captured, placed in camps, were being liquidated in camps in Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I had some pieces of -- individual pieces of information, but not official information. I had individual bits of information, and that's why I did take some measures in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you blamed those liquidations on paramilitary groups; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I cannot blame. Again, you're putting me in the situation of asking me. I'm not the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, so I have no intention of answering questions like that. Why I would answer when I was not the commander of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the question is put to you, and you should answer any question to the best of your knowledge if it is put to you. So therefore I now repeat the question: Do you or do you not blame those liquidations on paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paramilitary formations bear the bulk of responsibility generally in the entire Birac area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For -- for everything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So to quite some extent, you do blame the paramilitaries for those liquidations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did say for the most part. As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And specifically with regard to Zvornik, you're talking about such well-known paramilitary groups as the Yellow Wasps headed by Zuco Vuckovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: There were several of these paramilitary formations. That one was one of them. But I don't know specifically who committed these things. I cannot really say with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, General, I'm going to suggest to you that by pointing the finger at so-called paramilitary groups for these liquidations, you're doing something similar to what you were doing in calling the Zvornik TO independent. That is, you're ignoring their actual subordination. And the fact is that you were aware of the fact, for example, that these paramilitaries were supposed to be subordinated to the Zvornik TO and later the Zvornik Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I would like to remind you that these paramilitary formations in Zvornik did whatever they wanted. They even captured the president of the municipality, Mr. Grujic. So that was the ratio of strength in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, the fact is that these particular groups - specifically Zuco's group - was being paid by the Zvornik TO and later by the Zvornik Brigade, and they were subordinated. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. That is something that you have to ask those who were authorised to pay them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let me turn quickly to a couple of items then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First, 65 ter 32502. And if we could go to the last page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a TO payroll list signed by Marko Pavlovic, indicating payment to Zuca Vuckovic as a TO member for military activity between the 1st and 17th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm going to turn to another document quickly because we'll see quite a number of the same names in this document. That's 65 ter 32276.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a document, as you'll see in a moment, headed the 1st Infantry Battalion. And we'll see on page 4 of this document, in both English and Serbian, payment for salaries or of salaries for June 1992. We see the stamp of the Zvornik municipality on the top of the Serbian version. And on page 32 of the English -- 7 of the English and 32 of the Serbian -- no, excuse me, that's the wrong cite. 77 through 79 in the Serbian. We can see the references to the 1st Infantry Battalion and Zuca's group within that, including Vojin Vuckovic and his brother Dusan Vuckovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: English page 32, if I didn't make that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And a comparison of those payment lists will also indicate, as I mentioned a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: These are not the corresponding pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry. It should be 32 of the English and 77 through 79 of the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you say 77 through 79, you should indicate which one you want to have on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We'll start with 77 then. It is a confusing direction to the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And there we can see Vojin Vuckovic and Dusko Vuckovic and so on, scrolling down. And finally, if we could turn to 65 ter 18491, English page 7 and B/C/S page 32. This is the Zvornik Brigade duty book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And should be English page 7, Serbian page 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And as we see, we see the entry at 0530, Zuco's courier came, gave us the message that Zuco wants to know what to do next and whether he should come to the command. General, these documents, you'll agree, indicate that not only was Zuco's group supposed to be subordinated for the Zvornik TO and subsequently the Zvornik Brigade, but in fact they were; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know any of these documents so that I'm not -- I don't have an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I'll turn to some of the information you did have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But I'd tender those three documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 32502 receives number P7349. Document 32276 receives number P7350. And document 18491 receives number P7351.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7349 through P7351 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, in fact, General, contemporaneously, you were well aware of Zuco and the Yellow Wasps and in fact met them when they came to Kalesija in late May to participate in combat operations; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And at that time they were resubordinated to the Kalesija TO staff in order to engage in those combat operations in Kalesija; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, General, perhaps we can look at some of what was happening in other parts of the region beyond Zvornik. So let me look, in particular, at evidence this Court has received about what happened in Seher near Osmace on the 27th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I'll be referring to P2528, which is under seal in this case, Mr. President, but I'll do so in a manner that doesn't implicate the reasons for the confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But at least not to be shown --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or still to be shown but --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I think my friends can follow and therefore we don't risk comprising the confidentiality in any way. Yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, as I indicated, this concerns what happened in Seher which is near Osmace in what was part of the Kalesija municipality before the conflict. Can we --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. This is not broadcast, correct? Right. And -- I don't think this -- this shouldn't be on the -- there is no need to put this on the screen. Let's just move this off screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That evidence, as the Court has received, is that on the 27th of May, 1992, Serbs in military uniform and some in civilian clothing collected the Muslims of Seher together, separated the men from the women and children, and transported them to Osmace town. And from there, the men were transported to Paprace school gym, from there to the Vlasenica secondary school, and there from Susica, and ultimately onward to Batkovic in the case of this particular person. So once again as we saw in the case of Zvornik, the rounding up of the people from the village and separation of the men from the women and children and their placement in detention facilities. General, the collection of Muslims of Seher on the 27th May, 1992, the separation of the men from the women and children, the placement of those men in camps and detention facilities, that was the implementation of your order to move out the Muslims, separating the men from the women and children and putting the men in camps for exchange, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You issued an order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We didn't receive the full interpretation of the answer. Witness, could you repeat your last answer, please, and move a little bit further to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said no and I can also provide an explanation if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, the military forces operating in that area received an order from you the day before to do precisely that, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: The order was received, and if you allow me to do so, I shall explain. First of all --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, before you explain let's have the Court take a look at that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I call up P7086.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's an order dated 26th of May 1992 to the commander of the Light Infantry Battalion Osmace. That's your order, General, isn't it, and it's signed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot understand or hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again, perhaps the usher would assist in adjusting the microphone, if you are leaning towards... yes. Perhaps it should be moved slightly -- a little bit further. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the top it's not the brigade. It's the infantry battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm not sure what your point is there, General. I think that's exactly what I said. It's an order from you to the commander of the infantry battalion, Osmace, and it's your order and it's signed by you; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And it provided, among other things, in item -- now here looking at item 6: "Move women and children out of the Muslim villages to Kalesija and Gracanica whereas the men are to be taken away to collection centres." Now that meant move the women and children from the villages they inhabited to Muslim-held parts of the municipality of Kalesija and to Gracanica in the Zivinice municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes. But allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now you can explain.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: This order pertained to all, not only Muslims. Serbs were also moving out because this was a combat area. So at the same time Serbs left, went to Zvornik and Srbinje. In order to protect the people there, I ordered that women and children be allowed to go to Kalesija and Gracanica because of combat operations. Then also because of revenge. People, refugees were coming in from Gracanica, Kalesija, Tuzla, and we had to prevent any kind of revenge that could be taken by them, and that is why I have to say that it is precisely this order of mine that saved thousands of people. Had we left these people in the combat area, I believe that many would not be alive today. So it is precisely this order that contributed. And later on, we will see that the same persons were exchanged and that to this day they live together with their families.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, can you give us an order that was made similar to this one with respect to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the order specifically in Vlasenica, for instance. The Crisis Staff of Vlasenica. The very moment when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just listen to my question. Are you able to provide a written order similar to this one with respect to Serbs? Not asking you where it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right now, I cannot do that in writing because I have no ability to do so right now. But there were such orders precisely because of the combat operations taking place. Because that was a combat area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you a -- also a question in relation to this. Could you tell us how many Serb women and children were removed -- were moved out through this order from Muslim villages to Kalesija and Gracanica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Muslim villages? As for the municipality of Kalesija, practically the entire Serb population, women and children, they went to Zvornik and to Serbia. The only ones that stayed were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you how many Serbs, women and children, were moved out of Muslim villages and then taken to Kalesija and Gracanica? I'm not talking about any other villages. I'm talking about Muslim villages, how many Serbs were moved out from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Serbs were not being moved out. That was territory that was controlled by Muslim, so we cannot move Serbs out, can we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But you earlier said it would apply equally to Muslims and Serbs. But if only Muslims are living there, the effect is that it's only Muslims that will be moved out, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether -- well, from the combat zone, both Muslims and Serbs were moved out because that was basically a front line. We did not have any depth in our front, Mr. President. We did not have a -- a depth of the front. We just had the front line. So how could you control what was happening in depth? Just one example: A brigade defends 10 to 15 kilometres principle, whereas the zone of my brigade is 150 kilometres. 150 kilometres. Along one line, you have 100 kilometres in depth. You cannot prevent revenge. You cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's not what I asked. So this order specifically focused at moving out women and children from Muslim villages. That is to say, Muslim women and children. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, you told this Court just a moment ago that "practically the entire population" of the municipality of Kalesija was Serb. In that regard, let's take a look at 65 ter 025591.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me -- thank you. Thank you, Ms. Stewart. 65 ter 02559L.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that that is not what the witness said. It would be a good thing before showing this document to check whether the witness uttered those words; namely, that almost the entire population of Kalesija was Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll first read what is in the transcript. Perhaps you do that literally, and then if the first question to the witness is whether the -- whether there's any dispute about the way in which his words were reflected. And if the witness disputes it, then we'll be able to verify it on the basis of the audio. Mr. Tieger, I leave it in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm referring to page 60, beginning at line --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: "As for the municipality of Kalesija practically the entire population was Serb."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you go on further: "Women and children, they went to Serbia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, the first question is is that what you said. If there's any dispute about it, we'll listen to the audio and then we'll find out what you exactly said and have it all verified. Did you say --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not say that. Since in Kalesija the majority population is Muslim, whereas this pertained to the Serb municipality of Osmace or rather the Serb municipality of Kalesija, and specifically the place that the gentleman, the Prosecutor, was asking about. That's Osmace, Seher, what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your last sentence. Witness, could you repeat the last sentence which was not caught by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What the Prosecutor has been asking about, that is the Serb municipality of Kalesija; specifically Osmace, a location called Seher, with a minority Muslim population. And Kalesija is a majority --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Again, we didn't hear the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what the witness explained to us that he limited the Serb majority to a certain area of the municipality, but this is to be verified if that is not what the witness may have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, and that should be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In any event, Witness, let's look at how that part of Kalesija became almost entirely Muslim-free, as you indicated. So first we're looking at 65 ter 02559L. If we can blow it up slightly so that we can see the names, focusing on the municipality in the middle. Okay. There we see Seher and other indicated in green as a Muslim village. And we also see, for example, above it, Memici, correct? So we see Osmace in blue, indicating it's Serb. Then we see Mahala and we see Memici above that, right? The latter two indicated as Muslim municipalities. Now, those municipalities were "liberated"; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you referring to municipalities or --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Those villages were, in that part of the Kalesija municipality, were quote/unquote, liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I don't know which specific villages you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to 65 ter 32498. We'll return to the map in a moment. General, I presume you'll recognise this as a report on the occasion of marking the day of the establishment of the Drina Corps prepared by you --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- on the 30th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 3 of the English, and I believe page 3 of the Serbian as well. There is emphasis placed on the liberation of Kalesija. Indeed, the need to mention the liberation of Kalesija. And as we read further, we see a specific mention of the liberation of the village of Memici and the placing of the said village under our control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us an indication? I have not found it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's -- if you see the middle -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it. I see it. That's approximately in the middle of the page immediately after the Italics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, the reason that the Muslim village of Seher ended up in the Serbian municipality of Osmace, that is, the newly formed municipality of Osmace, is because it was liberated in the manner we heard described earlier, and the same fate befell Memici which was praised as liberation in your retrospective; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, in order to respond to this question, I would have to make an introduction. Otherwise, it is pointless to go on. This happened at the time when the army, in fact, did not even exist. Secondly, for your information, the TO, the Patriotic League of the municipality of Kalesija was established before anything was done in terms of organising the Army of Republika Srpska. The TO, the Patriotic League first attacked the Serb villages in the depth of the municipality Jeginov Lug -- please, Jeginov Lug, Sarska Basta [phoen], military columns --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, let's -- I gave you an opportunity to provide what you called an explanation about something else. But let's establish the facts first. First, on the 26th of May you gave an order to move out the Muslim -- the people from the Muslim village of -- from those Muslim villages, give the order to the Osmace forces, and that resulted in the rounding up of the villagers of Seher on the 27th of May; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, actually, I think the -- excuse me, General, I apologise, but the interpreters couldn't hear you. I heard you say -- answer in the affirmative, but if you could just repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps be the microphone adjusted again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness's microphone is off and other microphones are on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again, General, if you could repeat your affirmative answer. You said the answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: My answer was yes. But you didn't allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I said I would as soon as I was permitted to establish the facts. Memici was also a Muslim village in that part of the Kalesija municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: No. Half of the village was Serb and the other half was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The village of Memici --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's go back to 65 ter 02559L. We see visual representations of the demographics of those particular villages, green for municipalities which were exclusively or predominantly Muslim; blue for -- villages, rather, which are exclusively or predominantly Muslim. Blue, the corresponding colour for villages that are exclusively or predominantly Serb. Memici, as we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, we don't see anything. It's not on the screen yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apparently there are some computer problems which slow down what appears on our screens. There are two ways to resolve it. Either we ask the Prosecution to produce it another way on the screen, or the second is to take the break a bit earlier and try to fix it over the next 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm just checking quickly to see if we have a hard copy in colour that we can put on the ELMO. If not, we probably will have to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm told the alternative is for Ms. Stewart to put it up in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was what I had on my mind, as a matter of fact, Mr. Tieger. Not your hard copy on the ELMO. But let's see whether we can have it on the ELMO -- whether we can have it on our screens through Sanction. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again, we see Seher in green consistent with the evidence that I read out to you before. Osmace in blue, Mahala in green, and Memici in green. So according to the census of 1991, Memici was a predominantly Muslim village; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, the logic to some extent escapes me. I mean, the witness was telling us about half-half. Now, I only see predominantly one ethnicity or predominantly another, and the half halves, I don't whether you consider a 51 per cent majority predominantly or not, but otherwise there's no room for villages which are half-half or 52-48. So therefore could it be checked, perhaps. And parties, I take it, could agree on these villages, what percentage is given in the census. Because to further explore with the witness whether he is right or wrong on the half-half depends on what we find in the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President, we can do that. And I agree that, first of all, "predominantly" in the sense I was using it meant on either side of 50-50. I agree with you there was no room for a 50-50 in -- in the context of the bright line green-blue, but my point was basically what happened to that village in the context of the orders given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I let you continue there. But "predominantly" for me is something heavier than by majority. That's -- but that's perhaps my understanding of English language, right or wrong, but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Next fact, Witness. You said that in that portion of the Kalesija municipality that is clarifying or attempting to clarify your early remark, that part was essentially all Serb, and I'm suggesting to you that that part of the Kalesija municipality became predominantly all Serb after the military operations resulting from the orders given, for example, on the 26th of May, 1992; correct? That's what happened to those villages we see here.

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, if you say that it's that way, then I assume that you think that it is that way. However, do go back to the period from the 8th, 7th of May, when there were combat operations, when Kalesija, I mean, was placed under the control of the Territorial Defence, the Serb Territorial Defence, and then the 23rd, the Muslims put it under their control. So this village, Memici, that you are mentioning on the basis of my order, in fact, there were no inhabitants there. This was a combat position. So in that period of time, that is to say, we are fighting -- we are, in fact, fighting the enemy. So there were no inhabitants there at all. As for Seher, Seher is Serb and Muslim. So these are villages. Seher. Half Serb, half Muslim. People lived together. However, the very moment there was danger, that somebody would commit a crime, we decided on this. And I have to tell you that I'm proud of what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So that's your answer, General. You gave an order to move out Muslims who weren't there in order to protect them from revenge even though they weren't there. That's the answer?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: We're not understanding each other at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You said you gave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What Mr. Tieger puts to you is the following. If you say there was no one living there at the time because it was a combat zone, why give an order that women and children should be moved out if they were not there. That's the question Mr. Tieger puts to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I spoke specifically about the village of Memici because what was pointed out was the village of Memici and there was nothing. I mean, as for Seher, where it is mentioned that people moved out. Yes, the population was half Serb, half Muslim, and that was the objective, that these people be allowed to go to Muslim territory in order to save them because there was combat going on. And the Serb population from these villages had also left. They went to Serbia. I mean, I really don't know. Are we understanding each other?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll find out. We'll take a break anyhow. So that gives us 20 minutes to further prepare for a full understanding. We'll take a break, and we'd like to see you back at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness, Mr. Tieger, had you any chance to look at Memici and percentages?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'll be addressing that first thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And by way and as long as we're waiting, could I take the opportunity to tender 65 ter 32498. That was the retrospective of October 1993 that the witness indicated was his.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And also if I may, the Kalesija map which is 65 ter 02559L.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the map receives number P7353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then can we call up 65 ter 2559M, like master.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, a few minutes ago you indicated at page 66, line 12, that Memici was half and half; that is, half Muslim half Serb. And at page 69, line 4, that Seher was half Muslim-half Serb, or half Serb-half Muslim. And in that connection, I wanted to look at the 1991 census. If we look at this first page of 65 ter 2559M, we see Kalesija. And turning to the third page, we see a list of villages in Kalesija. And we see Memici listed --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Third page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did that page not upload?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is only two pages in e-court for the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go back to the previous page. Is there anything ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The Sanction option, I think, will ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we enlarge on the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: None of the villages are mentioned here yet and we expect them on the next page, which is the -- it's not the next page but two pages forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There with see Memici listed at line 16, and I'm pointing that out because we'll need that line reference to find Memici in the 1991 census, and we see Seher listed at line 28. And if we turn to the next page in that case, then we see the continuation of the data for those villages now for the 1991 census, and we see at line 16 the demographics of Memici: 1.318 Muslim, 167 Serb. And at line 28 the demographics for Seher: 915 Muslim, 267 Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, your information to this Court, your testimony to this Court, that those villages were demographically half and half Muslim/Serb, was simply wrong; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I accept that. Perhaps I misspoke. I did say the places were mixed. That's what I meant. Therefore, there were both Muslim and Serb inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender 65 ter 2559M.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that the extract which doesn't contain the page we need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. And I guess we -- well, we will make sure that the two critical pages are added to that 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Excerpt of the 1991 census including Memici and Seher, still to be uploaded, would receive what number, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P7354, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there are no objections, so once uploaded they will be admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as long as we're on this topic, because you've mentioned both the Serb municipality of Kalesija and the Serb municipality of Osmace, let me clarify for the Court what that means.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could call up 65 ter 32513.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before we do that. Witness, could I take you back to one of your previous answers. I asked you whether any Serb, Muslim or women were -- children or women were moved out, and you said in those Muslim villages there were no Serbs living there. Now although it was not half-half, here apparently there was a considerable number of Serb families living in those villages. Could you tell us whether they were moved out as well? Or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did say that. Perhaps you didn't understand that. The entire population was moved out, both Serbs and Muslims, because it was an area where combat was under way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a combat zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then I asked you how many Serbs were moved out, and you said there were no Serbs living there in those villages because they were Muslim villages. Now, again, my question now is, first of all, were, to your knowledge and do you have any details about the number of Serb women and children that were moved out? That's my first question. Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have anything specific about these two villages, but the information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. I was talking about these villages. Could you tell us how many Serb men were put in camps that were taken from those villages, because apparently there were Serbs living there as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbs were not taken to camps. They were taken by the Muslim [as interpreted] side to Tuzla. They were not taken to camps here but they moved to Zvornik and to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said they were taken by the Muslims? Let me just check.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they were allowed to move on their own; whereas, the Muslim men were put into camps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And because they possibly were soldiers of the other armed forces, is that your explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But a number of the men who were not able-bodied were released together with the women and children to go to Gracanica and Kalesija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were they exchanged or were they ... because earlier you told us that you'd now say they were released together with the women and children to go to Gracanica and Kalesija. But earlier you said that these men were free to go, so -- wherever they wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that that group of women, children, and those who were unfit for service were allowed to go freely. Whereas, the able-bodied men were placed in camps, and then later they crossed to Muslim territory through exchanges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Even if there were no prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, practically they were not prisoners of war. They were temporarily placed there. In the beginning, it was a collection centre, a place to accommodate all of those people who were there. And then later, practically they were all released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But there's no records of that, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are records. Later, we will speak about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if the Defence would be able to give us the relevant records of that, of course it would certainly assist in the evaluation of the totality of the evidence. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we have a report. We have a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I invited the Defence to do whatever they think would assist us. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I had indicate just a moment ago that we would look at your comments about the Serb municipality of Kalesija and the municipality of Osmace.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In context, if we could turn to 65 ter 32513 and turn -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, there we see it and we see Kalesija and Osmace bolded. Let's turn to the second page, please. The top portion of that map we see Kalesija, the municipality of Kalesija, as it existed before the war in its configuration. And beneath it, we see Kalesija after the war. And what we can see from that map is that a portion of Kalesija, the portion that, as it happened, included Seher, which was the subject of your May 26th order, as it was implemented on the 27th of May, and as we can see from the configuration Memici now in the Serbian municipality of Osmace. So, General, when you referred to Osmace before -- well, first of all, when you refer to the Serbian municipality of Kalesija, you meant that portion of the Kalesija municipality that pre-existed the war that had been designated for Serbian control by the Serbian authorities, and when you refer to Osmace, you mean that portion of the former Kalesija municipality that had been taken under control by the Serbian forces and that eventually became part of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Well, please, believe me, it's very difficult for me to answer today because you're not allowing me to explain anything. So I can see that you're the one who is speaking more here. Kalesija had 30- or 40.000 inhabitants. Out of that, only 7.500 were Serbs. In the depth of Kalesija, there are a number of Serbian villages --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch all the village names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, the blockade of those villages, specifically Jegino [phoen] Brdo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm stopping you again. If we need further explanations, whether it was logical to do what was done or not, that's not the question. The question is whether you referred in your testimony to certain parts of that municipality. Now again, if the parties would like to know whether there was any logic behind it, they will ask you. If they don't ask you, apparently it's not that relevant for the case which is before us. So please leave it to the parties what they'd like to know from you, and could you please now answer the question that was put to you by Mr. Tieger. If need be, Mr. Tieger will repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, you see the graphic representation in front of you. That is what happened as a result of the operations that we've been looking at; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I see Kalesija on the map from 1991. And I see Kalesija after the combat actions in 1992. So I don't know what you're asking me about. If that's it, then that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender 65 ter 32513.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7355.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, General, you became aware at the time --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I apologise. I hope that the -- this map is not in the context of my order. This map is from the 8th of May, 1992. The 8th, 9th, and 10th is what the map looked like. It looked like this on those dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether there's any relationship between these maps and your orders will be considered in the evaluation of the totality of the evidence before us. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I apologise. The Prosecutor cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. In re-examination, the Defence can ask you any additional questions which sheds a better light on your evidence. Don't worry about how we are dealing with all that. Just focus on answering the questions. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, you became aware at the time that as a result of the capture of many Muslims, facilities in which those people were being held were filling up; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And indeed you visited the Vlasenica secondary school where the witness whose testimony I referred you to earlier, the witness from Seher, was taken, and he stated that -- he described what it was like there in the secondary school at -- in P2528; fearful that anybody could be taken at any time from the gym and anything could happen, describing that most of the people had been beaten and were covered in blood and were unwashed, that people were weak from hunger, that they were exhausted and afraid, and he testified that you inspected the gym while he was there. And that's the truth, right, you did visit the gym while Muslims were retained there in late May 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit the gym while Muslims were retained there, sir?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Not while the Muslims were there, but I was there when the Serbs from Tuzla were exchanged to go to Brcko and it took place in that gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to 65 ter 325 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just an explanation. What -- against who were the Serbs being exchanged on that day when you were there? Who were they exchanged with? Because the Muslims were not there anymore, according to what you tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 27th of June, the Serbs from the Serb villages of Kalesija municipality, Jeginov Lug, Dumica, and Zolje Jajici were arrested, they were taken to the central prison in Tuzla. Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I stop you, please. You said when you visited the school, the Muslims were not there. You went there when the Serbs were being exchanged. I'm asking you on that day who were they being exchanged with, because the memories were not there. Just answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Muslims from Seher and Osmace. They were being exchanged for those Muslims. I personally was present when the Serbs came from those areas, and I saw that gym for the first time. The school gym. That was the first time that I saw it. I saw arriving mostly elderly men, and we gave Muslims in exchange for these elderly men who had come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But at that point in time, where were the Muslims? Were they still in the gym to be exchanged for the Serbs coming in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where were they then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They were in Susica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the very last couple of words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please repeat the last couple of words. You said they were in Susica. And what did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Susica. It was a collection centre, reception centre at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you never visited the gym or the school before that day. And on that day, there were no Muslims in that gym anymore. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me say this. When I came, there were no more Muslims at the school. So that was my first and last visit there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 65 ter 32505, please; e-court page 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, General Andric, this is in the context of questioning about the statement of another witness in the Karadzic case, that questioning was done in private session, who also spoke about your visit to the high school gym. And at e-court page 46, that is transcript 41687 of the Karadzic case, we see the following exchange: "Q. You visited the Vlasenica secondary school gym, the high school gym, yes, when it was holding Muslims? "A. Yes." That was the testimony you gave under oath in the Karadzic case; correct, General?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I went there only when Serbs were there. I don't recall ever being there when the Muslims were there. I did meet that group of Muslims at the school in Paprace together with Pahomije and the president of the municipality where I asked the bishop to make sure that the people are taken to their destination safely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a moment, if we may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: General, as a result of your awareness that the detention of Muslims was straining available facilities, you ordered that a camp in Vlasenica be set up and that camp was the Susica camp; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you order the establishment of the Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: Please, could I be shown that order so then I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: P190, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you first answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to explain to you that the order for organisation and the order on the establishment of a camp, that's not one and the same thing. When you say that you're organising something, then you're organising something that had already been established. And the Prosecutor should read the heading. What does it say? It says organisation only later. The heading says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even this Chamber usually does not say what the Prosecutor should say, and we also do not dictate what the Defence should ask. So refrain from telling the Prosecutor what to do. Did you order the establishment of Susica camp, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, paragraph 7 of your statement, General, states the following in its first sentence --

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: May I get that? May I take a look myself. There's nothing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, what Mr. Tieger is now doing, he's quoting from your own statement which you've given to the Karadzic Defence and which you said you had reviewed recently. He is quoting from that. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger. And would you refrain from again and again interfering in -- when questions are put to you. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It states that document there listed as P3240, that's the Karadzic number, of 31 May 1992 is my -- excuse me, that is -- is my order by which I ordered that a camp be established in Vlasenica, stressing that international rules must be applied and forbidding any ill-treatment or liquidation of the prisoners. I just quoted from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's, I think, meanwhile admitted into evidence. It was 65 ter P190, and it now has become ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Previously admitted as P190 in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And referred to by its Karadzic P number in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. It's an exhibit number. Yes. That's, of course, not 65 ter but exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So that's the first thing, General. And you state that in the statement which you recently reviewed and attested to in Court this morning. And if we turn to P190, that's your order of the 31st of May, 1992, providing in item 1 -- well, in -- it is: Pursuant to the decision of the Birac Serb Autonomous Region government which regulates the moving out of the Muslim population from the territory of the Birac SAR. I hereby order, one, set up a camp in Vlasenica and secure it in compliance with international regulations. So my question to you earlier, General, about whether or not as a result of your awareness of the fact that detention facilities were being strained with increasing numbers of captured Muslims resulted in your setting up or establishment of the Susica camp was based on, in part, what you said in your statement, and what you said in your 31st May order, 1992. Do you now disavow having set up the Susica camp by virtue of your order of the 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SVETOZAR ANDRIC
utterances.text: I do not deny that I organised the camp, but I deny that I established the camp. Establishing the camp is one thing and organising the camp is another matter. So these are two different notions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But, Witness, Mr. Tieger is asking you about the establishment. You are putting in the word "organisation." He says you ordered the establishment. According to this order here, you're saying: Set up a camp in Vlasenica and secure it in compliance with international regulations. And he's saying you ordered this establishment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't give answers for the witness. But if there's any -- I can imagine that if there's any translation issue, draw our attention to the fact that there's a translation issue. And if you say for that reason --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm not going to suggest anything because we've already dealt with this extensively. I would just like to ask the translation interpretation service to focus on item 1 of this order and to have this translated or interpreted verbatim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President. I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me cover one -- I'm going to cover both aspects of that, General, tomorrow as it appears. But before I do, I want to look quickly item 4, which provides that the prime minister of the Birac SAR is to establish contact urgently regarding negotiations on the exchange of prisoners. So -- and in fact, those exchanges took place and it was the Birac SAO government, according to you, which did that, right, or which undertook that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you come a bit closer to the microphone. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The government and later the army dealt with that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Mr. President. The last thing I'd mention is that the two missing pages were added to 65 ter 02559M, so I believe it can now be admitted fully as P7354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The number had been assigned already. One second, please. Before I make any mistakes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7354 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And in fairness to the witness, could then item 1 of this order be translated again. Be interpreted -- read and interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm happy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In response to the objection by ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the translation would be verified before we restart tomorrow, that would fully meet the wish of Judge Moloto. Witness, we'll adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Yes, but before you leave the courtroom, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever it may be about your testimony; that is, testimony given today or testimony still to be given tomorrow. If that's clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I -- I think the Chamber does understand the use of the words in paragraph 1. It will all be verified. May I remind you that in your summary, I don't know what language you used in B/C/S, but if you think it was not setting up, then the interpretation perhaps should be verified as well because in English it was role of the witness in setting up and not in organising. So please check for yourself what you said at the time, but if it adds to the confusion, I would have certainly --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- tried to -- to avoid that. We adjourn for the day. We resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 29th of April, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of April, 2015, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
